prs.title: feat(tally): count adjacent word pairs with --pairs
prs.head: feat/pairs
prs.author: dev
prs.body:
## Why
Some reports want the most common two-word phrases.

## What changed
- `--pairs` counts adjacent word pairs on each line.

## Scope
- Pairs stay within one line.

## Blast Radius
Only runs that pass `--pairs` change; the default output is untouched.

## Verification
- `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests`

reviews.author: copilot-pull-request-reviewer[bot]
reviews.body: Copilot reviewed 2 out of 2 changed files in this pull request and generated 2 comments.

comments.author: copilot-pull-request-reviewer[bot]
comments.body: `pair_counts` keeps each word's original case, so `The cat` and `the cat` count as two different pairs. `tally` lowercases every word, so `--pairs` disagrees with the single-word counts on the same file.

comments.author: copilot-pull-request-reviewer[bot]
comments.body: `zip(words, words[1:])` raises an `IndexError` when a line holds a single word. Guard the slice or switch to `itertools.pairwise`.
